# zarrow fuzzing: design and runbook

Deliverables in this directory ($S):

- `fuzz_infra.patch`: harness, supervisor, triage, seed tools, corpus, build steps, CI, docs.
  Green on its own (`zig build test`, `zig build fuzz-corpus`, 0.16 `zig fmt`) on both
  compilers: every seed that crashes the unfixed library is held back for the fixes patch.
- `fuzz_fixes.patch`: the root-cause fixes for the 10 findings, their regression seeds and three
  unit tests. Review it on its own; apply after the infra patch.
- `fuzz_findings.md`: what the first campaign found, `findings\` the reproducers and traces.

## 1. Model: Arrow C++'s setup, mapped to zarrow

| Arrow C++ | zarrow |
|---|---|
| one libFuzzer binary per reader (arrow-ipc-stream-fuzz, -file-fuzz, ...) | one harness `fuzz/fuzz.zig` (`zig build fuzz -- <target> ...`) with `runOne(target, allocator, bytes)` per target; the same function backs `std.testing.fuzz` tests |
| ValidateFull on every decoded batch; Status errors are fine | `validateFull` on every column; compute results must also validate with the right length, else `fuzz-invariant` panic |
| ASan/UBSan, rss / malloc limits | Debug / ReleaseSafe safety checks; a counting allocator per input (leak check, 256 MiB live cap = `fuzz-oom`), 1 MiB input cap, watchdog thread (`fuzz-hang`, exit 77), supervisor RSS cap |
| generate_corpuses.sh, arrow-testing reproducers | `tools/fuzz_import_seeds.py` (arrow-testing, Apache-2.0 NOTICE) + `zig build fuzz-gen-seeds` (zarrow writers re-encode every valid seed: plain / lz4 / zstd, stream / file, sliced batches) |
| OSS-Fuzz | `.github/workflows/nightly-fuzz.yml` (10 min per target, artifacts, triage in the job summary) + informational coverage-guided job |
| fixed reproducers in arrow-testing data/arrow-ipc-* | `fuzz/corpus/<dir>/regress-<hash>.bin`, replayed by `zig build fuzz-corpus` in CI |

Targets: `ipc-stream`, `ipc-stream-zero-copy`, `ipc-file` (batches + tensors), `array-layout`
(hand-built ArrayData trees from a byte recipe: validateLayout, validateFull, then compute),
`compute` (decode a stream, then slice / take / filter / concat with input-derived indices and
predicates on every valid column), `c-abi` (ArrowSchema / ArrowArray trees imported through the C
Data Interface, then compute, then export + re-import). The c-abi generator keeps the C ABI's
contract (pointers valid, buffers sized as the importer derives them: every buffer points into
one 72 KiB arena whose integers are 0..255 or -1, lengths < 256) and fuzzes everything else.

## 2. Probe: Zig's built-in coverage-guided fuzzer (`zig build test --fuzz`)

| | Windows | Linux (WSL Ubuntu) |
|---|---|---|
| 0.17.0 | `error: --fuzz not yet implemented for windows` | not run (no 0.17 Linux toolchain here). 0.17's test_runner has the fix for the 0.16 bug below (`writeErrorReturnTrace`), so Debug should work; the nightly job runs it as `continue-on-error` until confirmed. |
| 0.16.0 | same error | works headless with an iteration limit: `zig build fuzz-test --fuzz=300K -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` (~2M runs, 25.6 % coverage in 15 min). Debug fails to compile: `test_runner.zig:566: expected type '*const debug.StackTrace', found '*builtin.StackTrace'` (std bug in the fuzz path). |

Findings and limits:

- `--fuzz=N` is headless; `--fuzz` without a limit implies `--webui`.
- C sources in the fuzzed module are compiled with sanitizer-coverage calls the Zig fuzzer
  runtime lacks (`undefined symbol: __sanitizer_cov_trace_cmp1`...), so zstd/lz4 are linked
  from a separate static library (`zarrow-fuzz-codecs` in build.zig) for the fuzz module.
- A crash is saved to `.zig-cache/f/crash` in Smith format (u32 LE length + bytes):
  `tail -c +5 .zig-cache/f/crash > repro.bin` gives the harness input, which then replays on
  any OS with `zig build fuzz -- <target> replay repro.bin`. The engine found R6 within a
  minute.
- The report prints one coverage line per test step (named after the first fuzz test).

Decision: targets are `std.testing.fuzz` tests (`zig build fuzz-test`), run once by
`zig build test` everywhere and by the coverage-guided engine on Linux; the portable harness
below is the primary, CI-gating path.

## 3. Portable path (both compilers, both OSes)

```
zig build fuzz -- <target> replay <file|dir>...      # each input once; a crash names its file
zig build fuzz -- <target> run <N|Ns> --corpus <dir>... --out <dir> [--seed N] [--max-len N]
                                       [--alloc-cap N] [--timeout S]
zig build fuzz-install                                 # zig-out/bin/zarrow-fuzz for tools/fuzz.py
zig build fuzz-corpus                                  # replay fuzz/corpus through all 6 targets
zig build fuzz-gen-seeds                               # gen-* seeds from the valid ipc-stream seeds
zig build fuzz-test [--fuzz=N]                         # std.testing.fuzz targets
python tools/fuzz.py run --targets all --seconds 600 --out .fuzz-out
python tools/fuzz.py replay --target ipc-stream --out .fuzz-out <file|dir>
python tools/fuzz_triage.py .fuzz-out > triage.md
python -I tools/fuzz_import_seeds.py <arrow-testing checkout>
```

`run` loads the corpus (skipping inputs the supervisor marked in `<out>/skip/`), executes each
once, then mutates: erase / insert / bit flip / random byte / arithmetic and interesting
integers at widths 1-8 in either byte order / chunk copy / Arrow tokens (ARROW1, 0xFFFFFFFF
continuation, EOS, version and vtable patterns) / splice with another entry / byte repeats, 1-5
stacked per execution. Without coverage, an input joins the corpus (and `<out>/corpus/`) when its
feedback signature is new: error name, batch count, validateFull error, set of decoded type ids
(root type only for array-layout, whose type tree is the input). The input is written to
`<out>/current.bin` before every execution (positional write, no reopen), so any crash or hang
leaves its reproducer. Throughput: about 5-7k exec/s per target in Debug on this machine.

`tools/fuzz.py` (stdlib only) runs the harness in chunks; non-zero exit or signal = crash,
`fuzz-oom` / `fuzz-leak` panics = oom / leak, exit 77 or chunk overrun = hang, RSS over
`--rss-mb` = oom-rss. It saves `<sha1-16>.bin` + `.txt` per signature (kind + normalized panic
message + top 3 non-std frames; for leaks the error-return frames of the failing path), keeps the
smallest input, counts duplicates in `index.json`, marks the input in `skip/` and restarts.
Checked on Windows (crash, leak, oom, segfault, hang via `--timeout 0`, RSS via `--rss-mb 1`) and
on Linux (crash, leak, oom, general protection fault, run loop).

`tools/fuzz_triage.py` prints, per target, each signature with count, kind, message, smallest
reproducer, first 10 frames and the first `src/` frame as the suggested location.

## 4. Runbook (agents): docs/fuzzing.md

1. `python tools/fuzz.py --out .fuzz-out run --targets all --seconds 300`
2. `python tools/fuzz_triage.py .fuzz-out`
3. `zig build fuzz -- <target> replay <smallest.bin>` (a single-file replay also prints the error
   return trace of a rejected input); debugger: `zig build fuzz-install` then
   `gdb --args zig-out/bin/zarrow-fuzz <target> replay <file>` / `devenv /debugexe ...`;
   ReleaseFast check: `zig build fuzz -Doptimize=ReleaseFast -- <target> replay <file>`.
4. Fix the root cause in the shared function behind the trust boundary; never loosen
   validation or special-case the input.
5. `cp <smallest.bin> fuzz/corpus/<dir>/regress-<first 8 hex>.bin`, add a unit test when it
   states the rule better, run `zig build test && zig build fuzz-corpus` on 0.16 and 0.17, re-run
   the campaign for that target.
6. Valid Arrow rejected by zarrow is a compat gap: issue, not a regression seed.

## 5. First campaign (details in fuzz_findings.md)

- Replay of arrow-testing + seeds through all targets, then 3 min per target mutation on the
  base: 10 root causes (R1-R10), 7 of them memory-safety or DoS. All fixed in
  `fuzz_fixes.patch` with regression seeds; R1 (no flatbuffer verifier) alone accounted for 241
  of 287 signatures and for both coordinator-reported classes (enum panics A, OOB slice B).
- Six compat gaps (valid Arrow rejected) listed separately, not changed.
- After the fixes: every base reproducer, the whole arrow-testing IPC data set (no size cap)
  and the committed corpus replay clean on 0.17 and 0.16 (Windows and Linux); the post-fix
  campaign result is at the end of fuzz_findings.md.

## 6. Corpus and size

`fuzz/corpus/` holds about 1.4 MB: arrow-testing reproducers and integration fixtures up to
32 KiB (`at-*`, NOTICE with origin, revision and Apache-2.0), zarrow re-encodings (`gen-*`, at
most 16 KiB each), the 9 old hand-made seeds (moved to the new dir names), `regress-*`, and a
canonical stream / file (`zarrow-canonical.bin`) embedded by the std.testing.fuzz tests. Old
dirs `ipc-reader/` and `array-validate-layout/` become `ipc-stream/` and `array-layout/`; the old
harnesses `tools/fuzz_ipc_reader.zig`, `tools/fuzz_array_validate_layout.zig` and steps
`fuzz-ipc-reader` / `fuzz-array-layout` are replaced by `zig build fuzz`.

## 7. Apply

Your worktree is CRLF; the patches are LF. From the worktree root:

```sh
S='C:\Users\cable\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-cable-Documents-dev-zarrow--claude-worktrees-zig-0-17-migration-branch-f92e21\3ab19c71-6c26-4cbd-ba49-bd6ba48132fc\scratchpad'
sed -i 's/\r$//' build.zig README.md CONTRIBUTING.md docs/README-ZH.md .github/workflows/ci.yml \
  .github/workflows/nightly-fuzz.yml fuzz/corpus/README.md tools/fuzz_ipc_reader.zig \
  tools/fuzz_array_validate_layout.zig && git apply "$S/fuzz_infra.patch"
sed -i 's/\r$//' src/ipc/stream_reader.zig src/ipc/fbs_lite/builder.zig src/ipc/fbs_lite/verify.zig \
  src/array/array_data.zig src/array/array_ref.zig && git apply "$S/fuzz_fixes.patch"
zig build test && zig build fuzz-corpus
C:\Users\cable\tools\zig-x86_64-windows-0.16.0\zig.exe build test --cache-dir .zig-cache16
```

Both applies were tested this way on a CRLF copy of the worktree (section 8).

## 8. Verification done

- Infra patch alone and infra + fixes, on a fresh copy of HEAD 010b99a: `zig build test`
  (0.17 and 0.16), `zig build fuzz-corpus` (0.17 and 0.16, Windows; 0.16 Linux), 0.16
  `zig fmt --check` on every changed .zig file, `python -m compileall tools`.
- New unit tests fail on the base and pass with the fixes (corruption sweep panics, lying length
  returns OutOfMemory, run-end window index out of bounds).
- Every finding replays on a ReleaseFast base harness to classify severity.

## 9. Summary (apply order, commands, open questions)

1. Apply `fuzz_infra.patch`, then `fuzz_fixes.patch` (sed CRLF->LF first, section 7); commit separately.
2. Check: `zig build test`, `zig build fuzz-corpus` on 0.17 and 0.16 (`--cache-dir .zig-cache16`).
3. Campaign: `python tools/fuzz.py --out .fuzz-out run --targets all --seconds 300`.
4. Triage: `python tools/fuzz_triage.py .fuzz-out`; replay: `zig build fuzz -- <target> replay <file>`.
5. Coverage-guided (Linux): `zig build fuzz-test --fuzz=1M` (0.16: add `-Doptimize=ReleaseSafe`).
6. Re-seed: `python -I tools/fuzz_import_seeds.py <arrow-testing>`, then `zig build fuzz-gen-seeds`.
7. Open: confirm `zig build fuzz-test --fuzz` on Linux 0.17 Debug (nightly job is informational until then).
8. Open: zstd amplification bound is 32768x payload; exact frame-content-size check if that is too loose.
9. Open: fix compat gaps G1-G4 (negative vtable soffset, empty bodies, nested dictionaries, empty-buffer alignment); G5/G6 are policy.
10. Open: c-abi generator is shallow (contract-safe arena); a deeper generator or a C-side producer would reach more of the importer.

## 3. Portable path (both compilers, both OSes)

```
zig build fuzz -- <target> replay <file|dir>...      # each input once; a crash names its file
zig build fuzz -- <target> run <N|Ns> --corpus <dir>... --out <dir> [--seed N] [--max-len N]

zig build fuzz-corpus                                  # replay fuzz/corpus through all 6 targets
zig build fuzz-gen-seeds                               # gen-* seeds from the valid ipc-stream seeds

python tools/fuzz_triage.py .fuzz-out > triage.md
python -I tools/fuzz_import_seeds.py <arrow-testing checkout>

`run` loads the corpus (skipping inputs the supervisor marked in `<out>/skip/`), executes each
once, then mutates: erase / insert / bit flip / random byte / arithmetic and interesting
integers at widths 1-8 in either byte order / chunk copy / Arrow tokens (ARROW1, 0xFFFFFFFF
continuation, EOS, version and vtable patterns) / splice with another entry / byte repeats, 1-5
stacked per execution. Without coverage, an input joins the corpus (and `<out>/corpus/`) when its
feedback signature is new: error name, batch count, validateFull error, set of decoded type ids
(root type only for array-layout, whose type tree is the input). The input is written to
`<out>/current.bin` before every execution (positional write, no reopen), so any crash or hang
leaves its reproducer. Throughput: about 5-7k exec/s per target in Debug on this machine.

`tools/fuzz.py` (stdlib only) runs the harness in chunks; non-zero exit or signal = crash,
`fuzz-oom` / `fuzz-leak` panics = oom / leak, exit 77 or chunk overrun = hang, RSS over
`--rss-mb` = oom-rss. It saves `<sha1-16>.bin` + `.txt` per signature (kind + normalized panic
message + top 3 non-std frames; for leaks the error-return frames of the failing path), keeps the
smallest input, counts duplicates in `index.json`, marks the input in `skip/` and restarts.
Checked on Windows (crash, leak, oom, segfault, hang via `--timeout 0`, RSS via `--rss-mb 1`) and
on Linux (crash, leak, oom, general protection fault, run loop).

`tools/fuzz_triage.py` prints, per target, each signature with count, kind, message, smallest
reproducer, first 10 frames and the first `src/` frame as the suggested location.
